newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain warns Gibraltar still problem with Britain.
newsitem.headline: Spain warns Gibraltar still problem with Britain.

text.p: Spain's conservative government said on Friday it would continue to enjoy friendly relations with Britain following Labour's landslide victory, but that Gibraltar would remain a sticking point.

"We shall continue with those good relations, and naturally the question of Gibraltar, which is an obstacle in that excellent relationship, for Spain, will continue as it was," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told Spanish national radio.
Gibraltar has been an irritant in relations between Britain and Spain for many years. Spain insists that Britain hand back the colony which it seized almost 300 years ago.
However, Gibraltar was not an issue in Spain's press coverage of Labour's sweeping victory. Spanish dailies concentrated instead on the man behind the Labour party: leader Tony Blair.
The first five pages of left-of-centre daily El Pais focused entirely on Britain's elections, with the headlines: "The Labour earthquake" and "Tony Blair crushes John Major at the ballot box".
A commentary described Blair as "the chameleon that makes everybody happy", saying he knew exactly how to adapt his political colour to his audience.

Describing him as an accomplished actor, the commentary pointed out that acting ran through the veins of both Blair and his wife Cherie's families. Blair's grandparents were actors, while Cherie's father was an actor, the daily noted.

"There are at least two Tony Blairs. One is a cultivated politician that dines in Islington restaurants.....the other is a British patriot who enjoys sitting in front of the television with a can of beer in his hand," the daily said.

Right-of-centre daily El Mundo was similarly absorbed with the elections, running the headlines: "Historical victory for the Labour party", and "Tory distress while Wall Street greets the defeat with a strong rise in the pound".
The daily described Cherie as a "discrete political animal".
"Cherie is a political animal that affiliated herself to the Labour Party some 16 years ago and competed in the elections -- symbolically -- before she was married," El Mundo said.

The staunch conservative daily ABC, meanwhile, ran a full page colour photo of Blair on its front page, his arm in the air as if saluting with the headline: "The triumph of Labour's Blair puts an end to 18 years of conservative government in Britain".
However, they sympathised with former prime minister John Major, saying: "He has been a good leader, capable of bringing the national economy to an exceptional state of wellbeing".
Barcelona daily La Vanguardia, said the Labour Party would now be set free from the great expanse of desert in which it had lost the last four elections.
"It would be unjust to blame Major (for the conservative defeat). The conservatives are now paying for their long stay in power and above all their division," the daily said.
